title: Range Tools
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/0/bod: Bollinger Bands have three lines: the **middle band** is an SMA 20, and the **upper and lower bands** sit 2 standard deviations away from it. The standard setting is **20 and 2**. Since this lesson's charts are short, we used a period of **10**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/1/bod: In a range, being near the **upper band** means price is relatively expensive, and near the **lower band** means relatively cheap. A reversion trader looks to buy at the lower band and sell at the upper band, with the **middle band** as the first target.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/1/tip: Touching a band isn't a signal on its own. Wait for a reversal sign, like a pin bar.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/2/pro: Where's the last candle compared to the Bollinger Bands?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/2/exp: The last candle's wick reached the lower band, so price is stretched and cheap compared to the last 10 candles. In a range, this is where you start looking for a buy signal.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/3/sen: The standard Bollinger setting is a ___-period average with bands ___ standard deviations away.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/3/exp: John Bollinger's default setting is 20 and 2. On short charts you can lower the period, like the 10 in this lesson.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/4/bod: When the bands get **tight** (a **squeeze**), volatility has dropped and a big move is usually on the way, but you can't know its direction in advance. In a strong trend, price can also **walk the band**, touching it again and again. Selling the upper band there is dangerous.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/5/sta: In a strong uptrend, price can touch the upper band many times and still keep climbing.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/5/exp: In a strong trend, touching the upper band is a sign of strength, not of being expensive. That's why you should only read Bollinger signals as reversion signals in a range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/6/pro: Gold is ranging, and the last candle poked above the upper band with a long upper wick and came back. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/6/exp: In a range, poking above the upper band and snapping back with a long wick means buyers couldn't hold price up there. The first target is the middle band (around 2398), with a stop above the wick in case the range breaks.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/8/pro: In a range, price reached the lower Bollinger Band and printed a hammer. What's a sensible first target for a buy?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l1/steps/8/exp: Mean reversion means a return to the mean. The middle Bollinger Band is that mean, so it's the natural first target.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/0/bod: **RSI** swings between 0 and 100 and measures the strength of recent moves. Above **70** is called **overbought** and below **30** is **oversold**. The standard period is 14, but on this lesson's short charts we used **RSI 7**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/1/bod: In a **range**, RSI usually swings between about 30 and 70, and hitting 30 near the range bottom makes a buy chance stand out more. But in a **strong trend**, RSI can stay above 70 or below 30 for a long time.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/1/tip: Overbought means it's gotten expensive, not sell right now.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/2/pro: What does RSI show on the last candle?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/2/exp: After several bearish candles in a row, RSI dropped below 30. The recent selling was very strong, and price is near the range bottom.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/3/sen: Classically, RSI above ___ means overbought and below ___ means oversold.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/3/exp: The classic levels are 70 and 30. 50 is the middle of the scale, and 14 is RSI's default period, not a level.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/4/pro: Tap the candle where RSI went oversold (below 30).
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/4/exp: With this long bearish candle, RSI hit about 22, the only time it went below 30. After that, price returned to the middle of the range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/5/sta: When RSI goes above 70, you should sell right away.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/5/exp: RSI above 70 only says recent buying was strong. It means something in a range near the top, together with a reversal candle. In a strong trend, it can stay high for a long time.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/6/bod: If price makes a **lower** low but RSI makes a **higher** low, that's called **bullish divergence**: selling pressure is fading. Near the range bottom, this sign makes a bounce more likely. The opposite, near the range top, is **bearish divergence**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/7/pro: Near the range bottom, price made a lower low but RSI made a higher low. What does this show?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/7/exp: Price went lower, but the drop had less power behind it. That's bullish divergence: a sign a bounce is likely, not a guarantee.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/8/pro: USD/JPY reached the range top, RSI went above 70, and the last candle has a long upper wick. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l2/steps/8/exp: The range top, overbought RSI and a long upper wick together say buyers are tired. A move back to the middle of the range (around 150.00) is more likely. The top might still break, so you need a stop above the wick.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/0/bod: The best range trades come when several signs line up. Each extra sign nudges the odds up a little, but no combo is ever **certain**.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/1/bod: Say EUR/USD is ranging between 1.0800 and 1.0880. **Buy** near the bottom, put your **stop loss** just below it, **target 1** is the middle of the range and **target 2** is near the top. Many traders close part of the position at target 1.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/2/pro: USD/JPY has been ranging between 149.20 and 150.00, and you bought near the range bottom. Set your first target using the usual range-trading plan.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/2/exp: The first target is usually the middle of the range: (149.20 + 150.00) ÷ 2 = 149.60. Many traders close part of the position there and hold the rest for a second target near the range top.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/3/pro: GBP/USD is ranging between 1.2640 and 1.2740. You sell near the top at 1.2730, with a stop at 1.2750 and target 1 at mid-range (1.2690). What's the risk-reward to target 1?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/4/pro: The range runs from about 1.0800 to 1.0860. Tap the candle that gave the best sell signal at the range top.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/4/exp: This candle went above 1.0860 but closed below the top with a long upper wick (a pin bar), so sellers pushed price back. The other touches of the top had no reversal candle.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/5/sta: The middle of the range is a good place to enter a reversion trade.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/5/exp: In the middle of the range, a sensible stop is far away and the target is close, so you have no edge. Reversion trades make sense near the edges of the range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/6/pro: Put the steps of buying at the range bottom in order.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/6/ite: Confirm the range: flat top and bottom, flat average
Price reaches the range bottom and the lower band
Spot a reversal candle and oversold RSI
Enter with a stop just below the range bottom
Close part at the middle band, the rest near the top
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/6/exp: First the market type, then where price is, then confirmation. The stop goes in with the entry, and scaling out locks in profit.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/7/pro: Bitcoin reached the range bottom (58,500), touched the lower band, RSI is turning up from below 30, and the last candle is a hammer. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/7/exp: Four signs line up: the range bottom, the lower band, oversold RSI and a hammer. A move back toward the middle band (around 59,500) is more likely, but you still need a stop below the hammer's wick.
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/8/pro: Which setup is better for a reversion trader?
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/8/opt: Range bottom, lower band, RSI below 30 and a hammer
Mid-range, RSI at 50 and an ordinary candle
Right after a strong, high-volume break of the range bottom
Strong uptrend, selling at the upper band
lessons/mean-reversion-u2-l3/steps/8/exp: The first option has several signs pointing the same way at the edge of the range. The others either have no edge (mid-range) or the market isn't ranging anymore.
